payload.feature:
Close issue #219: a provider's limit refusal arrives after `accepted`, so a gate chain cannot fall to its next judge.

Read the issue, decision 0016 (the judge chain), decision 0041 ruling 3 (a gate whose judges are unavailable parks rather than descends), and the limits section of `docs/guides/agent-library.md`, which already names the fix.

**The defect, measured three times.** The claude driver answers `accepted` the moment the CLI spawns. The account's limit refusal (`rate_limit`, "You've reached your ... limit") arrives after that, and decision 0016 deliberately excludes a mid-session failure from fallback — so an exhausted limit stops every seat that opens on that vendor while the next judge in the chain sits idle. On run `decision-0046-enactment-slice-i--165601b4` the engine smith chained `fable@high -> opus@high` exited 1 twice with empty stderr (seq 3646/3652), both seat transcripts carrying `rate_limit`, and a probe seconds later answered `ok` on both `claude-fable-5-1` and `claude-opus-5`: the limit is per model, opus was serving throughout, and the chain's own second link would have taken the work. The same run parked this way once before in design (seq 2133). Two of that run's six parks are this bug.

**Build it so:**

1. **A provider's pre-session refusal is a determinate start failure.** No turn started, and a limit or auth error in the first records: the driver classifies it as a refusal to start, not as an accepted attempt that failed. The engine's chain then advances to the next judge exactly as it does for a model the machine cannot reach at all. A refusal that arrives after the first turn stays what decision 0016 says it is — this narrows nothing about mid-session failure.
2. **The classification is the driver's, per built-in adapter.** Claude first, because that is where it is measured; state in the code and in the guide what each other built-in adapter does with the same shape, and cover the ones whose wire protocol makes the same distinction available.
3. **The record keeps the refused attempt with its reason**, so the journal shows the chain descending and why, and neither the fold nor any readout invents a success.
4. **A test per built-in driver with a shim that refuses before the first turn**, alongside the existing conformance suite, proving the attempt is classified determinate and the chain advances.
5. **If enacting this needs a ruling** — because it reads on decision 0016's exclusion — write it as a numbered decision with status `proposed` and the context that forced the question, and index it. Never accept a decision; that is the operator's, in the file.

Constraints, binding: do not edit `contracts/*.v1..v8`, `realms.v1..v3`, `seat-record.v1..v3`, `policy/phase-machine.json`, `reference/`, or `fixtures/evaluator/corpus.ndjson`. Re-pin any witness or compose digest that moves. Any test driving a boxed step end to end skips under `BROKKR_HANDS_BOX`. Coverage is exact and literal.

Green before you finish: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, and both `brokkr compile --bundle bundles/self` and `--bundle bundles/verify`. Do not push and do not open a pull request; the operator lands it. Say what you could not verify and what evidence you relied on.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including all three operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Five platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew, Scoop and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
}
```

result.notes:
Reviewed 168ec7e + 25f2101 (and the 6808ca7 merge, which is clean: git diff a730f53..HEAD is only the 13 #219 files, nothing of #221 reverted). Gates run here and green: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast (0 failures across every suite, log in .forge/review-219-tests.log); brokkr compile --bundle bundles/self and --bundle bundles/verify. No frozen surface touched (contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, reference/, fixtures/) and no witness or compose digest moved. The design is sound and the tests are unusually honest: begins_work keeps 0016's boundary, the fold keeps reading past a classified refusal, deadline_killed (ruling 5) correctly holds a watchdog kill off the fail-to-start side, and a test per built-in adapter (claude, lanetally, codex, dsh, exec) drives a refusing shim. Decision 0053 is proposed, indexed, and states dsh's and exec's abstention with a reason.

TWO FINDINGS REMAIN, neither fixed by me (read-only seat).

1. MEDIUM (correctness). Buffering the transcript row silently breaks a documented invariant, and the two comments asserting it are now false. engine.rs:3539-3542 states that 'a driver's transcript locator reaches the record as evidence the moment its harness announces one, which is what lets an attempt killed on its deadline still hand its thread to the retry that follows', and adapters.rs:1023-1028 (codex thread.started, unmodified by this run) repeats it. Since this change, run_seat buffers the transcript checkpoint until a work-beginning row flushes it, and a SIGKILLed driver flushes nothing. For codex — the one built-in that declares resume — the exposed window is thread.started to the first turn.started/item row, which under the hands box spans MCP server startup and can be minutes. An attempt killed on its deadline in that window journals no transcript locator, so seat_session finds nothing and the operator's retry starts a cold, re-paid session. This bites exactly on ruling 5's own path: a hung first turn now parks (by design) and the retry that follows is the one that loses the thread. Decision 0053's Consequences discloses the live-drilldown effect of the same buffering but not this one. Wants either a disclosure + ruling in 0053 and correction of both now-false comments, or a design that keeps the locator journalable without putting a checkpoint on the refused attempt.

2. LOW (robustness). adapters.rs:2876 — the refusal branch consults neither exit_code nor whether the seat wrote a result, so any record the classifier reads as a refusal overrides a session that nonetheless succeeded, discarding the written result and reporting a determinate failure to start. Not reachable with the measured claude or codex CLIs (a successful session always emits at least one work checkpoint, which sets began_work), so this is defence-in-depth — but rate_limit_event is the one shape the decision table documents with no measurement behind it ('the lifecycle message newer CLIs emit'), and it is classified as a refusal rather than as a throttling notice. Gating the branch on a non-zero exit or an absent result file would cost nothing measured.

INFO, no action asked. (a) Two behaviour changes are real but disclosed in 0053 and both guides: a live drilldown cannot locate a seat's prose during a long first turn, and a driver that hangs its whole deadline before the handshake now parks instead of descending. (b) Security: the refusal reason carries up to 80 chars of token and 160 of provider prose into an append-only record. bounded_wire_line collapses whitespace, strips control characters and clamps both halves; the web console writes through textContent throughout ui.html with no innerHTML, so there is no terminal-escape or HTML injection path, and this is the same class of provider text the journalled stderr tail already carries. The classifiers read machine fields only — no prose sniff, decision 0001 respected — and the engine's predicate stays structural. No security finding at or above medium; no security-hold. (c) The landing_shape.rs commit.gpgsign=false fixture fix is unrelated test hygiene bundled into this run; harmless and commented.

COULD NOT VERIFY: the exact-coverage gate. scripts/coverage-exact.sh needs the pinned nightly-2026-09-05 through rustup, which this seat is not permitted to invoke, and its mktemp target directory would land on the /tmp tmpfs. Coverage of the new code is plausible by inspection — every arm of claude_refusal, codex_refusal, refusal_reason, bounded_wire_line, begins_work and transcript_locator, both sides of the turn-zero guards, and each accepted/flush path has a test — but the exact gate is unrun here and must be confirmed in CI. Remote CI on the final head is likewise unrun.

Returned implement on fire/219-limit-fallback: answered both findings the review left on 6808ca7, committed as fa56026 (signed, tree clean, not pushed).

MEDIUM (correctness) — buffering the transcript checkpoint silently broke a documented invariant and left two comments asserting it. A driver captures its harness's locator at the harness's first message (for codex, the thread id a retry resumes) and that row used to reach the journal at once, which is what let a deadline-killed attempt hand its thread to the retry after it. Since the withholding it is held until the first work checkpoint and a SIGKILLed driver flushes nothing, so a kill between `thread.started` and the first turn journals no locator, `seat_session` finds none, and the retry opens a cold session — and that is ruling 5's own path, where a hung first turn parks. I took the reviewer's first option, deliberately: the row must be SENT early to survive a kill and must NOT EXIST for the refusal to be structurally a fail-to-start, so at the driver the two cannot both hold. Decision 0053 gains ruling 8 naming the window (harness launch to first turn; under the hands box, MCP startup, minutes), the cold retry it costs, and what is unchanged outside it; Consequences say it too; and the Alternatives now record the one design that WOULD close it — move the hold into the engine, which survives the kill it orders and could flush a held row when its own watchdog fires, dropping it only for a classified refusal — with why it is not taken here (it puts a driver's `step` vocabulary inside the engine's journaling path and moves when the 0034 seat-record fence judges a held row). That is the operator's to rule on; I did not enact it. Both false comments now state the window: engine.rs `seat_session` and the codex `thread.started` arm. New test `the_pre_session_rows_are_held_until_the_first_turn_and_then_flushed_in_order` drives a codex shim through the window and pins that nothing reaches the engine before `accepted`, that the held rows flush in their own order, and that the locator is among them; the resume_tests case for an attempt that journaled no session now names ruling 8.

LOW (robustness) — the refusal branch read neither the exit code nor whether the seat wrote a result, so any record the classifier read as a refusal would discard a session that nonetheless succeeded. `began_work` catches every shape #219 measured, but `rate_limit_event` is the one row in ruling 3's table that is asserted rather than measured and the one a newer CLI could emit as an advisory. The branch now also requires `!delivered` (exit 0 and the result file present); ruling 7 states the rule and its binding names the shim. New test `a_refusal_never_discards_a_session_that_delivered_its_result` errs with no turn row, writes its result, and keeps it.

Also carried, from the same review's earlier residuals, because they sit on the lines I was already editing: the transcript locator was the one harness-supplied field the reason quoted without the wire clamp (decision 0032 bounds its LENGTH only), so a harness announcing `abc\n\u001b[2K…` could forge a second line and terminal escapes into a durable record — it now goes through `bounded_wire_line` like the token, its doc comment says why, and the locator test composes a hostile announcement and asserts the reason is one control-free line; 0053's Consequences now say a refused attempt emits no `<driver>-session-finished` row either (so readouts keyed on it, and any usage beside a refusal, are affected), not merely no transcript row; and driver-authoring.md documents `DSH_USAGE_SHIM` and `REFUSING_STDERR_SHIM` and corrects its shim count. agent-library.md's limits section carries the kill/cold-retry consequence and the delivery wall.

GATES RUN HERE, ALL GREEN: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast (64 suites, 0 failed); brokkr compile --bundle bundles/self and --bundle bundles/verify. No frozen surface touched — the diff is 4 crate files and 3 docs, nothing under contracts/, policy/, reference/ or fixtures/ — and no witness or compose digest moved (witness_digests.rs passes untouched; no argv, adapter declaration or tool policy changed).

COULD NOT VERIFY: the exact-coverage gate, for the same reason both reviews reported — this seat's shell refuses rustup, so the pinned nightly-2026-09-05 cannot be selected, and the script's mktemp target would land on the /tmp tmpfs. Reasoned by hand instead: the only new production branch is `!delivered` inside the refusal arm, and `delivered` itself is `exit_code == 0 && result file present`, whose three combinations are already exercised (non-zero exit tests, the obedient path, and SILENT_SHIM's clean exit with no result file); the new `!delivered` arm is taken both ways by the existing refusal tests and the new delivering shim. The clamped locator adds no branch. Remote CI on the final head is likewise unrun, and the fix is still unproven against a live exhausted account — the evidence is the shim suite plus the run transcripts quoted in the issue and in 0053's Context.

Reviewed a730f53..fa56026 (the run's own four commits; the merge only reconciles the shipped #221 landing_shape fixture). Gates I ran here: cargo fmt --check clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings exit 0; cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast 64 suites ok / 0 FAILED (.forge/review-tests.log, review-clippy.log); brokkr compile --bundle bundles/self and --bundle bundles/verify both compiled. Tree clean, nothing pushed, no PR. NOT VERIFIED: scripts/coverage-exact.sh — the seat is refused permission to run it, so the exact-coverage gate is pending an external result, as the release config's own instruction anticipates.

CORRECTNESS: all five framing items are delivered. The classification is the driver's (claude_refusal / codex_refusal, machine fields only, no prose sniff); the per-adapter table matches the code (claude+lanetally share the stream arm, codex classifies error/turn.failed before the first turn.started, dsh and exec state why they cannot); the refused attempt is Failed with no accepted and no checkpoint and keeps its reason plus a [transcript kind/locator] pointer; driver_conformance.rs drives a refusing shim per built-in plus the negative REFUSING_STDERR_SHIM for dsh/exec; decision 0053 is proposed and indexed. Ruling 5 is the important catch from the prior review: I confirmed deadline_killed is set only by the watchdog (process.rs:146), read after disarm/reap (process.rs:222), and is the predicate's fourth term (engine.rs:3688), so a hung first turn no longer walks the chain down every link. The began_work + delivered double wall closes the errs-then-works and errs-then-delivers shapes, and I confirmed every emitted checkpoint carries a step and that transcript.rs always stamps step=transcript, so the begins_work denylist cannot misread a row. Binding constraints held: the diff touches only crates/ and docs/ — no contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, reference/, or fixtures/. No digest moved (tree clean, both bundles compile). AttemptReport is not serde-serialized, so no contract or schema moves with deadline_killed.

SECURITY: no new unbounded journal surface. Every field the classifiers quote — token, HTTP status, prose excerpt, and the transcript locator — goes through bounded_wire_line (control characters stripped, whitespace collapsed, 80/160 clamp), and the suite drives an adversarial locator carrying a newline and an ESC[2K sequence. No masking regression: the refusal reason joins the same unmasked-harness-output class as the pre-existing stderr tail, and the secret::mask_bytes sites are unchanged. The change only widens fail-to-start (more fallback); it never turns a failure into a success, and no readout synthesizes one for a refused attempt.

RESIDUAL 1 (low, correctness/doc) — docs/guides/driver-authoring.md, the new deadline-kill row reads 'The run **parks**'. A Failed outcome is first retried inside the seat's max_attempts (engine.rs:581) and parks only when they are spent; the row immediately below it says exactly that for the other `failed` case. True at the default max_attempts: 1, misleading for a seat that raises it.

RESIDUAL 2 (low, security/journal privacy) — crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs, claude_refusal's `assistant` arm fires on isApiErrorMessage OR a top-level `error` string, then quotes /message/content/0/text into the journaled reason. On the measured #219 shape that text is the API error's own prose, which is fine. On the `error`-only half of that OR, a record carrying real content beside an `error` field would put up to 160 characters of model message text into the append-only journal, against the fold's stated privacy invariant ('never message text, thinking, or full tool inputs'). No known CLI emits that shape, and the `result` arm has no equivalent exposure because it can only fire when no assistant record was ever seen — so this is a widened guard, not a measured leak. Tightening the assistant arm to require isApiErrorMessage before reading content text would close it.

Neither residual is above low and neither blocks; both are the table's call, not mine.
